classes.desc: Artificers are inventive martial specialists who fight with tools, contraptions and gear of their own making.
Barbarians are fierce warriors who channel a primal fury into battle, shrugging off blows that would fell anyone else.

Storytellers, minstrels and silver-tongued wanderers who draw Occult magic from words, music and the hearts of their listeners.

Every tavern has heard a song that made the room fall silent, and every bard knows why. Words and music carry power, and a bard has learned to pull on the threads that bind a listener’s fear, courage and longing. A ballad steadies a shaking ally’s sword arm. A whispered verse sours an enemy’s luck. A single, perfect note can shatter glass, nerve or bone.

Bards draw their magic from the harmonies, magic phrases, and through sheer force of personality rather than study or faith, using Charisma as their spellcasting ability. Where a Wizard pores over spellbooks, a bard learns magic the way a musician learns a tune: by ear, by heart and by performing it for anyone who’ll listen. Their spells are spoken, sung and played, which makes a bard formidable in a crowded hall and helpless with a gag over their mouth.

In the depths of a crawl, the bard is the party’s voice and nerve. They talk their way past guards, read a rival’s lies, and keep tired companions on their feet when the torches burn low. They are rarely the strongest in a fight, but they are almost always the reason the party survives it.

classes.desc: Clerics channel Divine magic granted by their faith.
Druids draw Primal magic from the wild places of the world.
Fighters are masters of weapons and armor, trained to win any battle through skill, discipline and endurance.

feats.d:
Starting at 1st level, your martial training lets you push harder with each moment of combat.

Whenever you roll your Action Die, you gain 1 additional Action Point (AP). This bonus increases to 2 AP at 6th level and 3 AP at 12th level.

Points gained from Prowess can’t exceed your Max Pool. Any excess is lost.
You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty.

opts.d: While you are wielding either a Bow, Crossbow, or Firearm, you can make ranged weapon attacks at creatures within 5ft of you without disadvantage.
While you are wielding a Light weapon in each hand, whenever you make a melee weapon attack with a light weapon in your Off-Hand you may add your ability modifier to the damage roll.
While you are wielding a Two-Handed melee weapon in both hands, you ignore the Heavy Property if the weapon you are wielding has it.
While you are wearing a Helmet in addition to either being Moderately or Heavily Armored, you gain an additional +1 to your Armor Class.
Whenever you use the [color=#8e171c]Shield Bash[/color] weapon action, you can add your Strength Modifier to the Damage total. you gain an additional skill point in Shields.
Your unarmed strikes count as Light, costing 1 AP, and deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 AP to attempt to grapple it.
Choose a weapon Category of your Choice; Axes, Blades, Bows, Cudgels, Firearms, Polearms, Swords, Unarmed, Miscellaneous, or Shields, You gain a single skill point in that weapon Category.

feats.d: Starting at 2nd level, during Intense moments of duress and stress you’ll sometimes find your body is able to take on more than it can tolerate. During combat on your turn, you can expend 1AP to gain an additional 2 Action Points (AP) for your current turn, At the start of your next turn, you start with one less Action point and gain 1EP (Exhaustion Point). Once this Combat action has been used, it cannot be used for the next 3 rounds of combat.
Starting at 3rd Level choose one of the following Weapon Categories of your Choice; Axes, Blades, Bows, Cudgels, Firearms, Polearms, Swords, Special, Miscellaneous, or Shields

classes.desc: Monks are disciplined martial artists who turn body and spirit into weapons, striking with speed and precision.

feats.d: Starting at 1st level, your martial training lets you push harder with each moment of combat. Whenever you roll your Action Die, you gain 1 additional Action Point (AP). This bonus increases to 2 AP at 6th level and 3 AP at 12th level. Points gained from Prowess can't exceed your Max Pool. Any excess is lost.

Your Limbs count as light melee weapons, Your unarmed strikes count as melee weapon attacks. They deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage, and you can use either your Strength or Dexterity modifier for their attack and damage rolls. This damage increases to 1d6 at 5th level, 1d8 at 11th level and 1d10 at 17th level.

When you make an unarmed strike with your off hand, you add your ability modifier to its damage, letting your blows flow together in one seamless combination.
While your total Armor % is 30% or less, you count as Unarmored instead of Lightly Armored. While you are Unarmored, you add your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class.
You learn the following Combat Actions: Swift Step and Patient Strikes. You also learn the following Unarmed Weapon Actions: Haymaker, Sweep Kick and Flurry of Blows.

As a free action on your turn, you can enter a state of perfect focus. Until the end of your turn, using Unarmed Weapon Actions gives you no Exhaustion Points (EP), and you can use them more than once per turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Rest.

At the start of your turn, you can gain 2 Exhaustion Points (EP) to end one of the following conditions on yourself: Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Sickened or Stunned. You can use this feature even while Incapacitated.

classes.desc: Paladins are holy warriors who wield Divine magic in service of an oath.
Rangers are hunters and trackers of the wild places, deadly with bow and blade and at home far from civilization.
Rogues rely on cunning, stealth and precision, striking where enemies are weakest and slipping away before they can answer.
Sorcerers carry Arcane magic in their blood.
Warlocks bargain with otherworldly patrons for Occult power.
Wizards study Arcane magic and record their spells in a spellbook.
classes.langs: Two additional Languages of your choice

feats.d:
You cast spells by drawing on Arcane magic, using Intelligence as your 
spellcasting ability.

[color=#8e171c]Spellbook.[/color] You start with a spellbook containing [4] 1st-level Wizard spells of your choice. Each time you gain a Wizard level, you add [2] Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. You can’t learn a spell whose level is higher than your Wizard level. When you add a spell, it starts at Rank 0, or at Rank +1 if it’s from your Major or Minor.

[color=#8e171c]Copying Spells.[/color] When you find a Wizard spell on a scroll or in another spellbook, you can copy it into yours if its level is no higher than your Wizard level. It takes 2 hours and [25] (G) per spell level. Copying a scroll destroys it.

[color=#8e171c]Preparing Spells.[/color] After a long rest, choose a number of spells from your spellbook equal to your Intelligence modifier + half your Wizard level (rounded down, minimum 1). These are your prepared spells, and you can cast only prepared spells. Spells from your Major prepared and don’t count against this number.

[color=#8e171c]Casting Spells.[/color] Casting a spell costs the MP listed on the spell. You can spend Action Points in place of Magic Points.

[color=#8e171c]Improving Spell Ranks[/color]. You can spend skill points to raise a spell’s Rank, which unlocks its Rank benefits. Each Rank costs 1 skill point (2 for spells from your Opposing School).

[color=#8e171c]Spell Attacks and Saves.[/color]
[color=#b7791f]Spell Attack[/color]: d20 + spell’s Rank + your Intelligence modifier
[color=#b7791f]Spell Save DC[/color]: 8 + spell’s Rank + your Intelligence modifier

Choose one school of magic to be your Major. This is the school your wizard has studied most deeply.

[color=#8e171c]Major Spells.[/color] When you learn a spell from your Major, it starts at Rank +1 instead of Rank 0.

[color=#8e171c]Opposing School.[/color] Each school has an opposite, shown in the table below. 
The opposite of your Major is your Opposing School. Raising the Rank of a spell from your Opposing School costs 2 skill points per Rank instead of 1.

[table]
School | Opposing School
Abjuration | Evocation
Conjuration | Necromancy
Divination | Illusion
Enchantment | Transmutation
Evocation | Abjuration
Illusion | Divination
Necromancy | Conjuration
Transmutation | Enchantment
[/table]

Choose a second school of magic to be your Minor. Your Minor can’t be your Major or your Opposing School.

[color=#8e171c]Minor Spells[/color]. When you learn a spell from your Minor, it starts at Rank +1 instead of Rank 0.

At the start of your turn in combat, you can forgo rolling your Action Die. If you do, you gain Magic Points (MP) equal to your spellcasting ability modifier instead. (If your spellcasting ability modifier is 0 or less, you instead gain 1 MP.)

Starting at 12th level, when you use Arcane Channeling, you gain twice as many MP.

At the start of your turn in combat, whenever you roll your Action 
Die, you also gain Magic Points (MP) equal to half your spellcasting 
ability modifier (rounded up, minimum of 1).

Starting at 12th level, you instead gain MP equal to your full 
spellcasting ability modifier.
